title: Correcting the first Europe trip: Paris festival in 1948 with Panassie
summary: Stewart realizes his first European trip was the 1948 Paris festival organized by Panassie, with Garner, Bechet, Parker and Miles Davis, before the later England trip.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Uh-huh. Now when you were -- when we were talking before, you had said that you didn't go to Europe until the mid-'50s with Norman Granz, but in discussion, we discovered that --
That's right.
-- actually it was in 1948.
I suddenly remembered that we went in 1948 and that wasn't with Norman Granz. That was [Hugues] Pannassie, his last name was.
Oh, did you play -- then you played that--
In France.
That was the festival in Paris with that Paris festival Sidney Bechet played, his band. Charlie Parker had a band over there.
Yes, I think Charlie was on this thing.
The tour, like a show.
Sure, yes.
Yeah, a festival, kind of, and Betchet was on it, --
Sidney, right.
-- and I think Miles Davis had a band with Tadd Dameron and Kenny Clarke.
That's right, yes, come to think of it.
Yeah, I think that probably was the one.
That had to be it.
That was the first time you went to Paris?
That's the first time I went over to Europe, yes.
So then it was later that you went to England then?
Yes, right.
So that was Paris the first time.
That's right.
Right.
Yes.
Panassie, yeah, right, right. So you worked with -- you and Garner worked together.
On that show.
In that particular show, right. Now did you meet Panassier? You met Panassie..
Oh, yes.
What kind of a guy did he strike you as?
Oh, he was quite a fellow. He was a musical promoter and a nice fellow, yes.
Did he speak English well? Was he kind of --
He spoke English very well, yes.
Did you get a chance to talk to or meet many of the French bass players when you were over there?
I met a couple here and there. Of course, the way we were traveling and what have you, I didn't have too much time to spend, you know. But all in all, it was a beautiful situation.
Do you remember where you played? I mean, not so much -- if you don't remember the name of it, did you play like outdoors or indoors?
Indoors.
You played indoors.
In a sort of a music hall like -- music theater like -- yeah, I'm sure it was indoors.
Did many people turn out to hear it?
Oh, yes, yes, thousands.
(Laughter.)
All groves,
Groves?
(Laughter.)
How would you say that? I guess that's about right.
Yeah, groves of people. Yeah, that sounds good, that sounds good. Did you record over there?
Not at that particular time, no. That came later.
